I start every cabinet plan by listening. How do you cook? What do you reach for every day? Where do your pots, pans, and pantry items live now? Your routines tell me what your kitchen needs to do for you. Next, I take careful measurements so every kitchen cabinet fits your space the way it should. From there, I build a custom layout and help you choose materials that match your style, your storage needs, and your budget. I put the full scope in writing, so you know what we are doing before work begins. You get one contact who answers your questions and keeps the plan moving. I coordinate the installation and set the timing around your specific project, not a one-size-fits-all schedule. That keeps the process clear and helps keep your home livable while we work. We serve homeowners in Liberty Township, Mason, Blue Ash, and Lebanon who want a kitchen that works as well as it looks. Schedule your cabinet consultation today.

From the owner
A home renovation project often feels like a heavy undertaking because of the uncertainty surrounding material quality and construction timelines. Many homeowners in White Plains face the stress of choosing a contractor who might prioritize speed over durability. When a kitchen or bathroom remodel lacks solid structural integrity or uses subpar finishes, the home loses its appeal to future buyers and can lead to recurring maintenance issues. A&F HOME RENOVATION INC addresses these concerns by focusing on expert craftsmanship and the use of high-grade materials. We have spent 15 years refining our methods to ensure every project at 19 Highland Avenue meets specific standards of longevity. For example, a kitchen remodel might involve replacing outdated cabinetry with custom-fitted units and durable stone countertops. When we install these features, we focus on the layout to improve your daily workflow. A bathroom remodel could involve a full walk-in shower installation with waterproof tiling and modern fixtures. These specific upgrades do more than change the look of your home. They increase the resale value of your property by addressing the two most scrutinized rooms in any real estate listing. We help you avoid the frustration of unfinished projects or materials that wear out within a year. Our team manages the process from the initial layout to the final coat of paint. You can see our work and start your project planning at https://afharenovationinc.com/

The walls get all the attention in a shower remodel, but the door is what you touch every day. Here is the honest guide from BathPlanet of Oklahoma: a sliding glass door suits a tub-width alcove where a swinging door would hit the toilet; a pivot door gives the widest, cleanest entry when there is floor space to swing; a frameless panel opens up a small bathroom visually; and a curtain is the right call for a barrier-free entry or a tight budget that will upgrade later. A shower replacement in Sand Springs, OK from our West 2nd Street showroom includes that conversation, because the door, the shelving, the seat, and the wall pattern should be chosen together, not as afterthoughts. Everything installs in seamless, no-grout acrylic by licensed plumbing professionals, under a lifetime warranty on parts and labor. From the owner
A lot of homes in Lehi, UT, weren't built with extra square footage in mind—and as families grow or needs shift, that starts to show pretty quickly. One route homeowners take is a garage conversion, since the shell is already there and it skips a good chunk of the construction work a full addition would require. Others go vertical, either through a loft if the ceiling height allows it or by adding a second story when the yard doesn't leave much room to spread out. Open concept layouts are another option worth understanding—removing interior walls changes how a space feels and functions, though it does require a closer look at load-bearing structure before anything comes down. Sunrooms tend to come up too, especially for homeowners who want more usable space without going through a full remodel; they connect to the main living area and bring in natural light, which changes the feel of the whole floor. Each of these approaches works differently depending on the home's existing layout, lot size, and what the homeowner actually needs the space for. In Lehi, UT, where a lot of neighborhoods have similar floor plans, it's worth mapping out which option fits the structure before committing to a direction.

From the owner
A Historic Villa Park Home Gets a New Beginning This 1911 Craftsman in downtown Villa Park had a porch that was beyond repair. The roof was pulling away from the house, the original spindles were gone, and the structure had lost much of the character that made this historic home special. Our challenge wasn't simply to build a new porch—it was to create one that felt right for the architecture of the home. Working with an architect who understood the homeowners' vision, we designed a new 10' x 34' porch inspired by the home's early-20th-century character, including a centered staircase, four columns, black-and-white finishes, a standing-seam metal roof, tongue-and-groove pine ceiling, Trex Signature decking, and custom lighting. The homeowners also gained approximately 150 square feet of additional outdoor living space for relaxing and entertaining. Today, the porch has completely changed the home's curb appeal—and the homeowners say people walking by regularly stop to compliment the house. “I was the embarrassment of the town with my house looking like something out of Beetlejuice, and now that the porch is done, I can't even mow the lawn without getting compliments!” A historic home deserved a porch that felt like it belonged there. Classic Remodeling | Villa Park, IL

Finished Basement Home Gym in Glen Mills, PA | Custom Rubber Flooring, Mirrored Wall & Mini-Split Climate Control A recent home gym build-out we completed as part of a finished basement remodel in Glen Mills, PA — purpose-designed to give the homeowner a true full workout space without leaving the house. The entire room was built from a previously unfinished section of the basement: framing, insulation, electrical, HVAC, wall-to-wall rubber gym flooring, and a fully mirrored accent wall sized to the room. The mirror wall — installed in a single seamless run — instantly doubles the visual size of the space and makes form checks easy during free weight, cable, and spin work. Heavy-duty rubber athletic flooring runs corner to corner with full baseboard returns, designed to take dropped dumbbells, kettlebells, and bench loads without damaging the slab underneath. A ductless mini-split AC unit was installed and wired in to keep the gym comfortable year-round without overworking the main HVAC system, plus a dedicated wall-mounted TV with floating media shelf for streaming workouts. From the owner
Thinking about a bathroom remodel this fall? Cooler, drier Upstate SC weather makes autumn one of the best seasons to start — tile and paint cure faster, and subcontractors are less booked than in peak summer. Start by checking permits with Clemson Building Inspections and planning ventilation. Size your exhaust fan to the room, vent to the exterior, and use cement backer board and a waterproof membrane in wet zones to prevent mold. If you’re changing plumbing locations, budget extra time and check hot-water capacity — a tankless or larger tank may be worthwhile for larger showers. Choose durable finishes for our humid climate: porcelain tile, waterproof LVP, and marine-grade cabinet finishes stand up well. Consider low-threshold showers and reinforced walls now if you want greater accessibility later. Local knowledge matters. Working with a general contractor who understands Clemson permitting, climate, and material suppliers saves time and surprises. Tap Learn more for the full guide or reach out for a free estimate.

Spring is one of the best times to start planning a basement remodel, and the reason is simple: projects that begin now are typically ready to enjoy by late summer or early fall. A finished basement can add meaningful living space to your home without the footprint of an exterior addition, and when designed thoughtfully, it feels like a natural extension of your main floor. Whether you envision a family room, a home office, or a guest suite, the right planning makes all the difference. At Gentry Custom Remodeling, we approach basement finishing with the same level of care we bring to every project. Lighting, ceiling treatments, storage, and flow are all addressed early in the design phase so the finished space feels bright, comfortable, and genuinely livable year-round. We define every detail before construction begins, which keeps the build organized and on schedule. If your basement is currently underused square footage, now is the time to change that. Our team serves homeowners throughout Dublin, Powell, and Lewis Center, and we would love to help you turn that space into something your family actually uses every day.
